A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Meta-Causal Graph and Curious Causality-Seeking Agent research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and document organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original prediction, downstream reward, ablation and causal-graph recovery results in Chemical and Magnetic environments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, restricted-intervention tests, partial-observation experiments, intrinsic-reward comparisons and efficiency studies.

M1.justification: v3 introduces Adaptive Codebook Fusion and three alternative curiosity rewards, retaining edge entropy as the default. The mask loss changes from testing signed causal effects to thresholding their absolute magnitude. Appendix E also corrects the commitment loss to compare the encoder output with the codebook vector. These substantively revise the documented procedure and objectives; rerunning the retained results is not established.

E1.justification: The original Chemical and Magnetic coverage remains. v3 adds restricted-intervention manipulation tests with reduced magnetic force, increased ball density and additional friction (A.9, Table 4), plus Chemical tests where variables gradually become observable (Section 6.3, Table 8). These substantially extend tested environmental and observation conditions beyond the earlier corruption scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add Sandy-Mixture, spelled Sandy-Mixure in Table 1, and Transformer. Both receive prediction-accuracy and downstream-reward results. All original comparator rows remain, making this a limited expansion of the existing comparison set.

E3.justification: v3 adds training-budget comparisons using 10k–15k rounds for MCG and 25k–30k for GNN/MLP, and separate parameter-size comparisons (Tables 10–11). Restricted-intervention and gradual-observation experiments introduce additional evaluation designs. The original CEM and training configurations remain unchanged in renumbered Tables 6–7; the gradual-observation schedule is not specified.

E4.justification: New analyses test alternative curiosity signals (Table 9), robustness to restricted interventions and physical changes (Table 4), partial observability (Table 8), and whether additional training or parameters resolve baseline deficits (Tables 10–11). The original component ablations and codebook-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are conducted eight times. v3 retains ± reporting but removes the checklist statement identifying standard deviations. Its new efficiency Tables 10–11 report point values without uncertainty. No increase in repetitions or new statistical testing is documented.

E6.justification: Shared numerical rows in Tables 1–2 and existing empirical plots are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for new comparators and appendix studies. For example, Table 8 reports MCG accuracy of 73.52±9.56 versus FCDL's 63.75±13.75 at n=2 under the new partial-observation setting. This is newly reported evidence, not a same-setting improvement over v2.

T1.justification: Proposition 2 and Appendix A.10 introduce probabilistic encoder assignments and a derivation of misclassification probabilities under lossy representations, adding a substantial theoretical analysis. Existing identifiability theorems and proofs remain. Reachability theory already appeared in v2 Appendix A.8. The new approximation contains an unresolved disappearance of the sample-count factor n.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about compact context-dependent causal graphs, intervention-based identification, curiosity-driven exploration and empirical robustness. The revised title and abstract emphasize open-ended worlds, a scope already explicit in v2.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains how lossy representations can mix true meta states and interprets better representations as reducing misclassification. It also interprets the new observation and intervention tests as supporting applicability to evolving environments. Existing limitations concerning unreachable states and intervention budgets remain.

D1.justification: The code-access address changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. Appendix B.1 newly specifies random color initialization and a negative Hamming-distance Chemical reward, although that reward description is unreconciled with positive Table 2 rewards. Existing hardware, optimizer and CEM details remain; relocating the VQ-VAE exposition to Appendix E does not itself add information.

R1.justification: Section 5 expands causal-representation-learning coverage. New Sections C.3–C.4 explicitly distinguish the work from FCDL, attribute context-dependent causality to earlier research, and position MCG relative to factored/relational model-based RL and probabilistic graphical models. Additional references support these discussions. The earlier acknowledgment of FCDL's VQ-VAE approach remains in Appendix E.

P1.justification: Section 4 is substantially reorganized to lead with exploration, while the detailed representation-learning exposition moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix E. The method narrative is rewritten, dedicated comparison discussions are added, the title changes, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. These materially change document structure despite extensive retained text.

P2.justification: v3 adds six tables covering experiments and notation, expands and reorders Tables 1–2, and substantially compacts and rearranges Figures 6–9 into paired partition/matrix displays with revised captions. Existing empirical plots are retained. The changes extend beyond numerical updates or page renumbering.

improvement.justification: New comparisons, robustness tests and resource controls broaden the evidence, and Appendix E corrects v2's commitment-loss expression. However, v3 introduces a misclassification approximation missing its sample-count factor and a reward definition inconsistent with positive Table 2 values. New fusion criteria and observation schedules also remain underspecified. These empirical benefits and new rigor/reproducibility problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
